lines.text: You withdraw R20,000 from your savings pot. You don't get R20,000.
SARS adds the withdrawal to your income for the year, and taxes it at your normal tax rate.
Say you earn R25,000 a month. That's R300,000 a year, and you're under 65.
At that income, every extra rand is taxed at 26%.
So SARS takes about R5,200 of your R20,000.
That leaves R14,800. And your fund's admin fee comes off that too.
Owe SARS money? That's taken first, before you get paid.
And you can only withdraw once a tax year, from R2,000.
The full two-pot guide is on the channel. Follow for a new money rule every day.
So before you withdraw R20,000, work out what you'll really get.
